newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha tumbles, focus on Itochu suspension.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha tumbles, focus on Itochu suspension.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha fell sharply for the second consecutive day on Thursday, dragged down by overnight losses in crude oil prices, traders said.

News that South Korean petrochemical firms decided to stop buying naphtha from Japanese trading house Itochu Corp until April-delivery cargoes cast a bearish pall over the market, but the impact is likely to be limited as market levels were plunging anyway in line with crudes, traders said.
First-half February open-spec naphtha was assessed at $233.00/234.00 a tonne in late afternoon trade, down from $244.00/245.00 on Wednesday and $250.00/251.00 on Tuesday.
Traders said bidding in late Thursday trade was mostly notional, as potential buyers retreated to the sidelines in anticipation of further declines.
The backwardation in naphtha's inter-month spreads was a touch narrower, with offers for first-half February/first-half March heard at plus $9.50 against no firm bids.
Seven South Korean petrochemical companies said on Wednesday they would stop buying naphtha from Japan's Itochu, accusing the company of price manipulation.
Itochu officials were unavailable for comment.
